neighbours.label: imperative 'check' or 'see' telling the reader to consult or verify something
fire: Some pills contain aspirin, so check the label before you buy them.
For the full schedule of matches, see the table at the end of this page.
If you feel shaky, check your blood sugar right away.
You should check the tires every month before a long drive.
For details on the earlier storms, see the previous chapter.
Before planting, check the soil for moisture with your finger.
For the history of the bridge, see the article on the old town.
Always check the expiry date on the carton before drinking the milk.
quiet: Some pills contain aspirin, and the label lists it near the bottom.
From the top of the hill you could see the stadium at the end of town.
If you feel shaky, it might be because you skipped lunch.
The mechanic wrote a check for the new tires last month.
We could see the earlier storms coming from far away.
Before planting, my grandmother waters the soil with a bucket.
From the tower I could see the bridge over the old town.
The carton of milk had been in the fridge for a week.

notes: Card peaks: ' check' (check the label, you should check, check your blood sugar), ' see'/' See' (see Tornadoes of ...). The + pole is first-person 'wanna see what I got' / 'below'. Near misses use see/check as ordinary verbs or nouns.
